question: What is the actual mainland distance of India from east to west?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2933 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The actual mainland distance of India from east to west is approximately **2933 kilometers**.
 
• This distance is measured between the easternmost point, **Arunachal Pradesh (Kibithu)**, and the westernmost point, **Gujarat (Ghuar Mota)**.
 
• The geographical extent of India lies between **68°7' E longitude** (west) to **97°25' E longitude** (east).
 
• India's geographical spread from east to west plays a significant role in its diverse climate, culture, and agricultural patterns.
 
• This vast expanse contributes to India having multiple time zones geographically, but the country follows a single standard time (Indian Standard Time, IST).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India’s Geography and Strategic Significance**

 
 
• India is the 7th largest country in the world, with a total area of approximately 3.28 million square kilometers.
 
• The country is bordered by the Arabian Sea on the west, the Bay of Bengal on the east, and the Indian Ocean to the south.
 
• The **north-south extent** of India (from Kashmir to Kanyakumari) is approximately 3214 kilometers.
 
• India’s geographical diversity also includes the Himalayan mountain ranges in the north, the Thar Desert in the west, and the coastal plains in the east and west.
 
• The vast geographical diversity contributes to India’s rich cultural, linguistic, and biological diversity.
